cs0019.title: CS0019
cs0019.short: The operator cannot be applied to those two operand types.
cs0019.summary: The combination of types on the left and right sides is not defined for that operator.
cs0019.why: Comparison and arithmetic operators are only available for supported combinations of operand types.
cs0019.tips: Check the two types shown in the error and confirm that both operands were converted to the types you intended.

badNotes.3: The result type and the comparison target type do not match

goodNotes.2: Convert the string to int so the types match

cs0021.title: CS0021
cs0021.short: Indexing with [] cannot be applied to this type.
cs0021.summary: This appears when [] is used on a value that is not an array and does not provide an indexer.
cs0021.why: int represents a single numeric value and does not provide elements that can be accessed by index.
cs0021.tips: Check whether the value is actually an array, List, Dictionary, string, or another indexable type.

cs0117.title: CS0117
cs0117.short: The type does not contain the specified member.
cs0117.summary: This often appears when code references a static member that does not exist on the named type.
cs0117.why: Console does not define a member named PrintLine.
cs0117.tips: Check spelling and capitalization, then inspect the actual member names offered for the type.

badNotes.1: Console has no member named PrintLine

cs0120.title: CS0120
cs0120.short: An instance member is being used through the type name without an object.
cs0120.summary: This appears when a non-static field, property, or method is accessed without an instance.
cs0120.why: Value belongs to each Counter object, not to the Counter type as a whole.
cs0120.tips: If the value truly should be shared by all instances, reconsider the design and whether static is appropriate.

badNotes.6: An instance property is accessed through the type name

cs0136.title: CS0136
cs0136.short: A local variable name conflicts with a name in an enclosing scope.
cs0136.summary: This appears when a nested scope tries to redeclare a local variable name that is already in use in an enclosing scope.
cs0136.why: C# prevents nearby scopes from using the same local name for different variables because it would make references ambiguous and confusing.
cs0136.tips: Rename the variable or check whether a second variable is necessary at all.

badNotes.4: This redeclares the same name x used by the outer scope

goodNotes.4: Use a different name to avoid the conflict

cs0161.title: CS0161
cs0161.short: A value-returning method has a path that does not return a value.
cs0161.summary: A method whose return type is not void may reach the end without returning a value on every possible control-flow path.
cs0161.why: When x <= 0, no int return value has been defined.
cs0161.tips: Trace every branch through if, switch, try, and similar constructs and confirm each path returns a value.

badNotes.3: Only this branch returns a value

goodNotes.4: Provide a return value for the remaining path

cs0165.title: CS0165
cs0165.short: A local variable may be used before it has been assigned.
cs0165.summary: Local variables must definitely receive a value before code reads them.
cs0165.why: If the condition is false, x is read without ever being assigned.
cs0165.tips: Give the variable an initial value or assign it on every possible branch before use.

badNotes.4: x may be read while still unassigned

goodNotes.1: Initialize x when it is declared

cs0200.title: CS0200
cs0200.short: Code is assigning to a read-only property or indexer.
cs0200.summary: This appears when code tries to write to a property that has no accessible setter.
cs0200.why: A property with only get cannot be modified from outside the type.
cs0200.tips: If the value is intentionally read-only, changing the assignment code is usually better than adding a setter.

badNotes.7: Name has no setter but is being assigned

goodNotes.3: Add a setter only if the property is meant to be mutable

cs0266.title: CS0266
cs0266.short: An implicit conversion is not available; an explicit conversion is required.
cs0266.summary: Conversions that may lose information, such as some numeric conversions, are not performed automatically.
cs0266.why: Converting double to int can discard the fractional part, so the code must make that intent explicit.
cs0266.tips: Decide whether a cast is really correct or whether Convert or an explicit rounding operation better expresses the intended behavior.

badNotes.2: double cannot be implicitly converted to int

goodNotes.2: Use an explicit cast to state the intent

cs0411.title: CS0411
cs0411.short: The type arguments for a generic method cannot be inferred.
cs0411.summary: The compiler does not have enough information at the call site to determine concrete types such as T.
cs0411.why: With no argument providing type information, the compiler has nothing from which to infer T.
cs0411.tips: Specify the type argument explicitly or provide an argument whose type allows inference.

badNotes.2: There is no information from which to infer T

cs1002.title: CS1002
cs1002.summary: This appears when a semicolon is missing where C# expects one, commonly at the end of a statement.
cs1002.why: Many C# statements are terminated with a semicolon.
cs1002.tips: The missing character may be on the line immediately before the location reported by the compiler.

badNotes.1: The statement is missing its trailing semicolon

cs1026.title: CS1026
cs1026.summary: This appears when parentheses in a method call, condition, or expression are not properly closed.
cs1026.why: There is no ) matching an earlier (, so the compiler cannot parse the following syntax correctly.
cs1026.tips: Check matching parentheses and reread the expression starting from the nearest opening parenthesis.

cs1061.title: CS1061
cs1061.short: The type has no matching member or extension method.
cs1061.summary: This commonly appears when code calls a property or method that does not exist on the object's type.
cs1061.why: string does not have an instance property named Count.
cs1061.tips: Check the type, member name, using directives, and the namespace required by any extension method you expect to use.

goodNotes.2: Use Length to get the number of characters in a string

cs1501.title: CS1501
cs1501.short: No overload accepts the supplied number of arguments.
cs1501.summary: The method name exists, but none of its overloads match the number of arguments in this call.
cs1501.why: The compiler cannot find a method signature that matches the argument list.
cs1501.tips: Inspect the available overloads and check both argument count and argument types.

badNotes.1: There are not enough arguments for the format items

goodNotes.1: Pass the required number of arguments

cs1503.title: CS1503
cs1503.short: An argument cannot be converted to the parameter type.
cs1503.summary: The number of arguments may be correct, but one of their types does not match the method definition.
cs1503.why: Print requires an int, but a string is being supplied.
cs1503.tips: Read the reported argument number and compare the source and destination types shown in the error.

badNotes.2: A string is passed where int is required

cs1513.title: CS1513
cs1513.summary: This appears when a class, method, if block, or other brace-delimited block is not closed.
cs1513.why: The compiler cannot find the end of a block that was opened earlier.
cs1513.tips: In a large file, automatic formatting can make the unmatched brace easier to locate.

cs1525.title: CS1525
cs1525.short: An invalid token appears where an expression is expected.
cs1525.summary: This appears when a symbol or keyword is used in a position where it cannot form a valid expression.
cs1525.why: The + operator requires a value or expression on its right side, but * appears there by itself.
cs1525.tips: This error can cascade from an earlier syntax mistake, so fix the first compiler error before chasing later ones.

badNotes.1: A standalone * cannot appear immediately after +

goodNotes.1: Replace it with a valid expression

cs7036.title: CS7036
cs7036.short: A required argument was not supplied.
cs7036.summary: The call is missing an argument for a parameter that has no default value and therefore cannot be omitted.
cs7036.why: No value is supplied for y, and y has no default value.
cs7036.tips: Add the missing argument, or define a default value only if omitting that parameter is valid by design.

badNotes.2: There is no argument for the required y parameter

cs0131.title: CS0131: Assignment to a nonassignable expression
cs0131.short: The left side of an assignment does not identify writable storage.
cs0131.summary: CS0131 appears when code tries to assign to a computed value rather than a variable, writable property, or indexer.
cs0131.why: left + right produces a result but no storage location that the assignment can update.
cs0131.tips: A [[variables-assignment|variable assignment]] must target actual storage. Store the computed result in a variable first, or write through an appropriate property or indexer.

badNotes.3: The addition result is a value, not an assignable storage location

goodNotes.3: Create a variable to hold the computed value
goodNotes.4: A variable is a valid assignment target

cs0104.title: CS0104: Ambiguous name references
cs0104.short: More than one imported namespace provides the referenced type name.
cs0104.summary: CS0104 appears when the compiler finds multiple accessible symbols with the same unqualified name and cannot choose one.
cs0104.why: Both First and Second contain Widget, and importing both namespaces introduces competing candidates for Widget.
cs0104.tips: The [[using-directive|using directives]] make both names available. Qualify the type with its namespace or introduce a clear using alias.

badNotes.4: Widget could mean either imported type

goodNotes.1: Give one fully qualified type a local alias
goodNotes.3: The alias makes the intended type unambiguous

cs0051.title: CS0051: Parameter type accessibility mismatch
cs0051.short: A method is more visible than one of the types in its parameter list.
cs0051.summary: CS0051 reports inconsistent accessibility when callers can see a method but cannot name a parameter type required by that method's signature.
cs0051.why: Api.Send is public while Request is internal, so code outside the assembly could discover Send but could not form its required argument type.
cs0051.tips: Align the [[access-modifiers|accessibility boundary]] deliberately: make the contract type public, or reduce the method's visibility when the operation is internal.

badNotes.1: Request is visible only within its assembly
badNotes.5: A public signature exposes the less-accessible Request type

goodNotes.1: Request is now as visible as the public method
goodNotes.5: Every caller that sees Send can name its parameter type
